title: FloodGuard Insurance-to-Value Credit on Building Limit Increases
content:
On the FloodGuard Private Flood Policy, a building limit increase that brings the building limit close to the building's replacement cost earns an insurance-to-value credit on its additional premium.

**Rule.** An insurance-to-value credit reduces the additional premium by 5 percent when the new building limit is at least 0.80 of the building replacement cost on file; by 2 percent when it is at least 0.60 but below 0.80 of that replacement cost; and by nothing below 0.60 of it.

## Questions the rule answers

**Which limit is compared?** The new building limit recorded on the limit-increase entry — the limit after the increase, not the limit before it.

**Compared with what?** The building replacement cost on file for the policy.

**What happens exactly on a line?** Each line is met by equality: a new limit equal to 80 percent of the replacement cost takes 5 percent; a new limit equal to 60 percent takes 2 percent.

**A hypothetical building.** The replacement cost on file is 400,000. Eighty percent of it is 320,000 and sixty percent is 240,000.

| New building limit | Share of replacement cost | Credit |
|---|---|---|
| 320,000 | 80 percent | 5 percent |
| 319,000 | just below 80 percent | 2 percent |
| 240,000 | 60 percent | 2 percent |
| 239,000 | just below 60 percent | none |
| 450,000 | above the replacement cost | 5 percent |
